spec.astemes_lib_lunit-2.0.13.6.spec: [Package] Name="astemes_lib_lunit" Version="2.0.13.6" Release="" ID=1128f93b19f22c892907a7079d2ffe98 File Format="vip" Format Version="2017" Display Name="LUnit" [Description] Description="LUnit is a LabVIEW Unit Testing Framework built on the xUnit unit testing model and inspired by JKI VI Tester. LUnit helps you test driving your LabVIEW development and provides the following key features.\0A\0A- Fast test execution\0A- Clear and informative results view\0A- Run specific tests quickly from right-click menu\0A- Test results visible directly in LabVIEW project explorer\0A- Instant loading of UI\0A- Parallel test execution managed by framework\0A- LabVIEW API\0A- Support for extenssion through add-ons\0A\0ALUnit is integrated into the LabVIEW development environment and the functionality is accessed through the Tools->LUnit menu. From the menu, you may create a new tests or open the LUnit UI to run tests. Tests may also be executed directly from the project explorer by right-clicking on a Test Case and selecting Run Test Case... from the menu.\0A\0AFrom Quick Drop window (ctrl+space) use:\0A - Ctrl+L to run all tests within active project\0A - Ctrl+Shift+L to run all test cases with tests calling into the current VI\0A\0AThere are a few examples installed with LUnit and these may be found through the NI Example Finder using the keyword LUnit. The examples are installed at C:\\Program Files (x86)\\National Instruments\\LabVIEW 20XX\\examples\\Astemes\\LUnit by default.\0A\0ADocumentation is available on https://lunit.astemes.com." Summary="Unit testing framework for LabVIEW" License="MIT" Copyright="Copyright (c) 2020, Astemes" Distribution="" Vendor="Astemes" URL="https://lunit.astemes.com" Packager="Anton Sundqvist" Demo="FALSE" Release Notes="With the release of LUnit 2.0, the requirement for test names to begin with the prefix `test` was removed. This has been the most asked for feature since the release of the toolkit, and now we have a stable implementation without compromising performance.\0A\0AThis change is non breaking, and LUnit 2.x can still run tests developed in LUnit 1.x and vice versa.\0AHowever, tests without the `test` prefix will not be discovered in LUnit 1.x and the toolkit will need to be updated to run these.\0A\0AWith the move to 2.x, the reporting plugin design has been updated and improved. This include minar changes to the interface. If you have made custom report plugins for LUnit 1.x, you will need to upgrade these for LUnit 2.x.\0A\0A\0AFix issue #12, #37 - Remove requirement for "test" prefix for test methods\0AFix issue #29 - Support for Cobertura code coverage report through plugin\0AFix issue #42 - Inconsisten aggregated results when broken test run from API\0AFix Issue #43 - Fix xml report inconsistency when using Skip.vi to\0AFix issue #46 - Limit recursion depth when using diff tool on large data structures\0AFix issue #47 - Edge case where running a vi could cause results to be reported twice\0AFix issue #48 - Edge case where modal window could prevent shift press from being captured by UI\0AFix issue #49 - Test ordering in UI reflects ordering in Tes Case lvclass\0AFix issue #50 - Improved readability of descriptions when comparing clusters - no more xml mess\0AFix issue #52 - Support for running only failed methods using the parameterized test add-on\0AFix issue #56 - Support for running multiple report types simultaneously\0AFix issue #57 - Aborting Parallel tests now stops immediately\0AFix issue #60 - Fix Suite result inconsistency if failed result followed by skip\0A\0AAdditionally, the test discovery has been improved significantly which makes the UI even snappier.\0AThe improved test cache mechanism improves load time for the Parameterized add-on." [Package]
Name="labview_open_source_lib_epoch_datetime"
Version="1.3.0.8"
Release=""
ID=e3641dbc83ba4c168aebaab187987619
File Format="vip"
Format Version="2017"
Display Name="Epoch Date & Time"


[Description]
Description="Epoch Date & Time is a unified time library for LabVIEW\0D\0A\0D\0AThis library provides support for UTC, Unix and GPS Epochs, enabling the conversion of timestamps into the proper frame of reference. It supports leap seconds to accurately convert from UTC (coordinatad universal time) to GPS (global positioning system) with proper offset based on divergence between UTC and TAI (international atomic time). It is completed with an extensible interface for Date-String formatters and comes pre-loaded with ISO8601 and RFC5322 support.\0D\0A\0D\0A- ISO8601:2019 is the international standard for date and time on almost every modern interoperable systems and databases. (RFC3339 strings can be read with non-strict ISO validation flag)\0D\0A- RFC5322 is the standard for email headers format, which includes a Date-Time string. This library covers only the date-time string part of the standard.\0D\0A\0D\0AEpochs\0D\0AUTC epoch starts on 1904-01-01\0D\0ALocal System is referenced to UTC with a time offset (from -14:00 to +12:00)\0D\0AUnix epoch starts on 1970-01-01\0D\0AGPS epoch starts on 1980-01-06\0D\0A\0D\0AKeywords: \0D\0ALeap Year, leap second\0D\0AUTC Time zone offset\0D\0AISO8601, RFC5322, Epoch\0D\0AGPS, Unix, UTC, Local System Time\0D\0A\0D\0AExample:\0D\0ATaking the following date and time: January 1st, 2021 @ 11:50:22.587 in Montreal:\0D\0A\0D\0AUTC DateTime = 2021-01-09T16:50:22.587Z\0D\0ANon UTC DateTime = 2021-01-08T11:50:22.587-05:00\0D\0AISO Date = 2021-01-09 or 20210109\0D\0AISO Calendar month = 2021-01\0D\0AISO Week = 2021-W01\0D\0AISO Week-Day = 2021-W01-6\0D\0AISO Ordinal Date = 2021-009\0D\0AThe reverse operation (ISO8601 DateString to Timestamp) supports all the above accepted formats, validates the input string for compliance and returns the ISO Format type matched.\0D\0A\0D\0ARFC3339 Format\0D\0ARFC3339 is based on ISO8601 but allows for a few deviations. A notable one is the space to replace the "T" in the UTC DateTime. Instead of providing an entirely separate method, the DateTime to Timestamp exposes a "Strict ISO?" terminal which can be set to false to accept RFC3339 format as a valid date-time string.\0D\0A\0D\0ARFC5322 Format\0D\0ANeeded for HTTP1.1 Support. Allows backward compatibility with RFC850 and ANSI-C time formats.\0D\0A\0D\0ACompare Timestamps\0D\0ABecause of the high resolution of the LabVIEW Timestamps, and the limited resolution of date-time strings, validation of equality needs to be performed with a certain precision. A practical method has been added to the palette to compare with a pre-defined resolution. The node defaults to 1 millisecond, but can be set to any fractional of multiple of 1, and units available span from nanoseconds to weeks. For simplicity, months and years have been ommitted because of extra computation required to handle leap years and different month lengths. All comparisons are performed in timestamp epoch (UTC).\0D\0A\0D\0AGPS, TAI and UTC\0D\0AGPS clocks and International Atomic Time are continuous and evenly-spaced, whereas UTC compensates for the fluctuation of Earth's rotation to keep the "year" synchronized for human activities. Therefore, leap seconds are sometimes added or removed to UTC time. Based on the history of the number of leap seconds added to the UTC, one must use this look-up table to make the exact time conversions. Leap Seconds record is kept in a table maintained by an international consortium (https://www.ietf.org/timezones/data/leap-seconds.list)\0D\0A"

[Description]
Description = "The JKI State Machine is a template you can use for quickly creating your own LabVIEW applications. This is the very same template that is used by the JKI team, nearly every day, and is the result of years of refinement by our team of LabVIEW experts. We encourage you to post any questions or comments to the JKI Software Forums. There you will find an active community of JKI software users, as well as JKI team members.\0D\0A\0D\0AHow to use:\0D\0A\0D\0AFind the JKI State Machine in the palettes\0D\0A1) Functions >> JKI Toolkits >> JKI State Machine\0D\0A\0D\0AUse QuickDrop to place a JKI State Machine on the block diagram\0D\0A1)  Press Control+Space then type "JKI"\0D\0A2) choose the "JKI State Machine" option that appears\0D\0A\0D\0ALaunch the JKI State Machine Explorer by either\0D\0AA) Right-click on a State String, Case Structure, or Event Structure to launch JKI SM Editor\0D\0AB) Press Control+Space then Control+J when you're on the block diagram of a VI containing a JKI SM\0D\0A\0D\0A\0D\0AUsing the Right-click menu on the JKI SM Parts for increased productivity:\0D\0A- Select an item in the tree to make that frame visible\0D\0A- Click back and forward to navigate the history\0D\0A- Drag and drop frames to reorganize the order\0D\0A- Right-click on items in the tree-view to rename, duplicate, delete, etc.\0D\0A- Right-click on a state string and choose Goto State Frame to jump to that frame of the JKI SM.\0D\0A- Right click on a state string or frame and choose Find Callers to find all callers of a state\0D\0A- Right-click on a bundle or unbundle by name and choose Find Data Accessors to find all accessors of the data.\0D\0A\0D\0ASpecial thanks to Jim Carmody for open sourcing his CaseSelect tool as a launching off point for the JKI SM Editor."

New State Enqueuing VIs:, to make it easier to conditionally enqueue states based on boolean logic and periodic timing (in a way that produces readable code).\0D\0A2. Improved Error Handling: to include information about the state where the error occurred as well as clear (or handling) "warnings" (non-zero `error code` but `status` is False).\0D\0A3. [Package]
Name="labview_open_source_lib_epoch_datetime"
Version="1.3.0.8"
Release=""
ID=e3641dbc83ba4c168aebaab187987619
File Format="vip"
Format Version="2017"
Display Name="Epoch Date & Time"


[Description]
Description="Epoch Date & Time is a unified time library for LabVIEW\0D\0A\0D\0AThis library provides support for UTC, Unix and GPS Epochs, enabling the conversion of timestamps into the proper frame of reference. It supports leap seconds to accurately convert from UTC (coordinatad universal time) to GPS (global positioning system) with proper offset based on divergence between UTC and TAI (international atomic time). It is completed with an extensible interface for Date-String formatters and comes pre-loaded with ISO8601 and RFC5322 support.\0D\0A\0D\0A- ISO8601:2019 is the international standard for date and time on almost every modern interoperable systems and databases. (RFC3339 strings can be read with non-strict ISO validation flag)\0D\0A- RFC5322 is the standard for email headers format, which includes a Date-Time string. This library covers only the date-time string part of the standard.\0D\0A\0D\0AEpochs\0D\0AUTC epoch starts on 1904-01-01\0D\0ALocal System is referenced to UTC with a time offset (from -14:00 to +12:00)\0D\0AUnix epoch starts on 1970-01-01\0D\0AGPS epoch starts on 1980-01-06\0D\0A\0D\0AKeywords: \0D\0ALeap Year, leap second\0D\0AUTC Time zone offset\0D\0AISO8601, RFC5322, Epoch\0D\0AGPS, Unix, UTC, Local System Time\0D\0A\0D\0AExample:\0D\0ATaking the following date and time: January 1st, 2021 @ 11:50:22.587 in Montreal:\0D\0A\0D\0AUTC DateTime = 2021-01-09T16:50:22.587Z\0D\0ANon UTC DateTime = 2021-01-08T11:50:22.587-05:00\0D\0AISO Date = 2021-01-09 or 20210109\0D\0AISO Calendar month = 2021-01\0D\0AISO Week = 2021-W01\0D\0AISO Week-Day = 2021-W01-6\0D\0AISO Ordinal Date = 2021-009\0D\0AThe reverse operation (ISO8601 DateString to Timestamp) supports all the above accepted formats, validates the input string for compliance and returns the ISO Format type matched.\0D\0A\0D\0ARFC3339 Format\0D\0ARFC3339 is based on ISO8601 but allows for a few deviations. A notable one is the space to replace the "T" in the UTC DateTime. Instead of providing an entirely separate method, the DateTime to Timestamp exposes a "Strict ISO?" terminal which can be set to false to accept RFC3339 format as a valid date-time string.\0D\0A\0D\0ARFC5322 Format\0D\0ANeeded for HTTP1.1 Support. Allows backward compatibility with RFC850 and ANSI-C time formats.\0D\0A\0D\0ACompare Timestamps\0D\0ABecause of the high resolution of the LabVIEW Timestamps, and the limited resolution of date-time strings, validation of equality needs to be performed with a certain precision. A practical method has been added to the palette to compare with a pre-defined resolution. The node defaults to 1 millisecond, but can be set to any fractional of multiple of 1, and units available span from nanoseconds to weeks. For simplicity, months and years have been ommitted because of extra computation required to handle leap years and different month lengths. All comparisons are performed in timestamp epoch (UTC).\0D\0A\0D\0AGPS, TAI and UTC\0D\0AGPS clocks and International Atomic Time are continuous and evenly-spaced, whereas UTC compensates for the fluctuation of Earth's rotation to keep the "year" synchronized for human activities. Therefore, leap seconds are sometimes added or removed to UTC time. Based on the history of the number of leap seconds added to the UTC, one must use this look-up table to make the exact time conversions. Leap Seconds record is kept in a table maintained by an international consortium (https://www.ietf.org/timezones/data/leap-seconds.list)\0D\0A"

[Package]

Format Version = "2017"
Display Name = "JKI State Machine"

[Description]
Description = "The JKI State Machine is a template you can use for quickly creating your own LabVIEW applications. This is the very same template that is used by the JKI team, nearly every day, and is the result of years of refinement by our team of LabVIEW experts. We encourage you to post any questions or comments to the JKI Software Forums. There you will find an active community of JKI software users, as well as JKI team members.\0D\0A\0D\0AHow to use:\0D\0A\0D\0AFind the JKI State Machine in the palettes\0D\0A1) Functions >> JKI Toolkits >> JKI State Machine\0D\0A\0D\0AUse QuickDrop to place a JKI State Machine on the block diagram\0D\0A1)  Press Control+Space then type "JKI"\0D\0A2) choose the "JKI State Machine" option that appears\0D\0A\0D\0ALaunch the JKI State Machine Explorer by either\0D\0AA) Right-click on a State String, Case Structure, or Event Structure to launch JKI SM Editor\0D\0AB) Press Control+Space then Control+J when you're on the block diagram of a VI containing a JKI SM\0D\0A\0D\0A\0D\0AUsing the Right-click menu on the JKI SM Parts for increased productivity:\0D\0A- Select an item in the tree to make that frame visible\0D\0A- Click back and forward to navigate the history\0D\0A- Drag and drop frames to reorganize the order\0D\0A- Right-click on items in the tree-view to rename, duplicate, delete, etc.\0D\0A- Right-click on a state string and choose Goto State Frame to jump to that frame of the JKI SM.\0D\0A- Right click on a state string or frame and choose Find Callers to find all callers of a state\0D\0A- Right-click on a bundle or unbundle by name and choose Find Data Accessors to find all accessors of the data.\0D\0A\0D\0ASpecial thanks to Jim Carmody for open sourcing his CaseSelect tool as a launching off point for the JKI SM Editor."
Summary = "JKI State Machine"
License = "BSD"
Copyright = "Copyright (C) 2005-2024, JKI"
Distribution = ""
Vendor = "JKI"
URL = "http://jki.net/state-machine/"
Packager = "JKI"
Demo = "FALSE"
Release Notes = "What's New in JKI State Machine 2024\0D\0A\0D\0AThis is a major new release with a focus on a few significant improvements:\0D\0A\0D\0A1. New State Enqueuing VIs:, to make it easier to conditionally enqueue states based on boolean logic and periodic timing (in a way that produces readable code).\0D\0A2. Improved Error Handling: to include information about the state where the error occurred as well as clear (or handling) "warnings" (non-zero `error code` but `status` is False).\0D\0A3. Upgrading source code to LV2020: to make it easier for community members to contribute and for the development team to take advantage of newer LabVIEW features.\0D\0A4. FIX: JKI State Machine Helper support for LabVIEW 2024Q (and greater)\0D\0A\0D\0AThere are also some other nice improvements to the template and misc fixes.\0D\0A\0D\0AUpdates to JKI State Machine Editor."
